text:
Aisha Patel: Quick design check — proposing a small IA regroup and breadcrumb + URL contract change. Idea: regroup sidebar into Observability / Models & Deployments / Workspaces / Billing, add a compact breadcrumb row above page header (Workspace > Models > model-name > revision) and use URL search params to represent panel state instead of relying on hash fragments. Thoughts? :eyes:

Tom Reyes: :eyes: High level makes sense. Two quick concerns: back/forward behaviour with params, and canonical links for sharing. How do you see history entries being emitted?

Jules Martin: I sketched a few flows — short version: prefer search params for nested panel state because hashes get messy when we introduce SSR and server routes. Params are easier to canonicalize and parse on the server, but we need a canonicalization layer so share links don't include transient flags. Also agree on shorter breadcrumb labels (eg. 'Models' rather than 'Model Management').

Samir K.: A11y nits: when the breadcrumb updates we should announce the change with a polite live region. Also ensure the skiplinks ("skip to main panel") land on the active right-hand panel rather than the left nav. Keyboard users must be able to jump directly into the current panel content.

DesignBot: Reminder: run accessibility sweep on any nav changes — check focus order, tab stops, aria-current usage, and visible focus ring.

Aisha Patel: Example URLs I imagine: ```
https://console.redwood.ai/w/acme/models?panel=history&version=v2
https://console.redwood.ai/w/acme/models/model-xyz?revision=42
```Using search params keeps the path stable (good for routing) and lets us encode panel + substate without adding lots of nested paths.

Tom Reyes: If we go params we must: 1) ensure server-side canonicalization strips ephemeral params, 2) decide which params are user-shareable vs local UI state (eg. ephemeral debugging flags shouldn't be in the permalink). Also prefer truncated breadcrumb labels with full id in a tooltip — long slugs blow up the UI.

Jules Martin: Agree on tooltip/truncation. For breadcrumbs: make them actionable (click to switch panels) rather than only navigational; that reduces need to use the left rail for quick jumps. UI-wise we'll show a chevron + truncated name, hover shows full name and copy button.

Samir K.: Keyboard/ARIA: breadcrumbs tabbable, last crumb gets aria-current="page", each crumb needs accessible name that reads the entire path ("Workspace: ACME, section: Models, item: model-xyz, revision 42"). Avoid opening flyouts on focus — open on explicit Enter/Space to avoid focus traps.

Aisha Patel: Action items: 1) Dev spike to validate SSR + param canonicalization (Tom), 2) Design mock for compact breadcrumb with truncation, tooltip and live-region announcement (Jules), 3) A11y checklist + skiplink acceptance tests (Samir). Can we aim to have spikes/mocks by next Wed? :calendar:

Tom Reyes: :thumbsup: I'll add a short engineering doc in eng-platform about canonicalization rules and history entries.

Jules Martin: I'll upload Figma mocks and 3 copy variants for the breadcrumb text — will post link here when ready: <https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/breadcrumb-batch>

DesignBot: Pinned: A11Y checklist and task #NAV-45 created in /tasks.
